slots.label: Ending: The Last Light
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Leave the Abyss with both companions alive, trusting you.

What happens: Daylight. Real daylight, sharp as a blade, and all three of you stagger into it with your hands over your eyes. Lyra laughs until she cries. Bror drops to his knees, kisses the dirt, then pretends he was checking it for quality. … You survived … dawn… in the dark. It taught you what a single one is worth.

slots.label: Ending: Dawnwalker
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Survive at least five dawns, then follow the light out with your party.

What happens: You stopped counting dawns somewhere after …. The thread of light grew into a staircase, then a doorway, and then a morning that had no idea what you carried. Lyra and Bror walk out beside you, squinting, alive. The villages above will call you Dawnwalker. Nobody will know you earned it a single thread at a time.

slots.id: Cutscene: Ending: A Door Left Open
slots.label: Ending: A Door Left Open
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Leave early, at a dawn, with both companions beside you.

What happens: You follow the light up and out long before the Abyss is finished with you. It isn't a victory. It's a door left open, and no one calls it cowardice, because no one else came back at all. Lyra and Bror don't ask what you left behind. They're just glad of the sky.

slots.label: Ending: Elegy For Lyra
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Escape with Bror after Lyra has fallen.

What happens: Bror carries Lyra's dagger up the last stairs and doesn't speak until the sun is full on his face. "She'd have hated it in her eyes," he says. A long silence. "She'd have loved the rain." Months later, you hear someone humming off-key in a tavern, and it takes you a full minute to realize it's you.

slots.label: Ending: Elegy For Bror
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Escape with Lyra after Bror has fallen.

What happens: Lyra walks beside you, and every few steps her hand drifts to where Bror's shoulder should be. At the surface she plants his axe in the earth like a headstone. "Somebody should hum," she says, and she does, badly, until the sun is all the way up. The dwarves of Karak-Dun never learn what became of him. Lyra tells the story to anyone who'll sit still.

slots.label: Ending: The Lonely Champion
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Escape after losing every companion.

What happens: You emerge alone. The sunlight is obscene. Nobody to squint with, nobody to laugh with, nobody to blame. Lyra and Bror are somewhere in the dark behind you, and the story the bards will sing has a happy ending that you'd trade, note for note, for one more bad joke around a fire.

slots.label: Ending: Bitter Parting
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Leave with a companion whose trust in you has withered.

What happens: The surface is bright enough to hurt, and it lights every crack between you. … stops at the gate. "I followed you down here. I don't think I can follow you anywhere else." There's no fight. That's the worst part. By dusk you're walking alone with a pack that still smells like their fire.

slots.label: Ending: Borrowed Souls
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Escape with a companion you resurrected.

What happens: You walk out together, but … sometimes stops mid-sentence, listening to something no one else can hear. You paid the Abyss echoes to bring them back. It never forgets what it's owed, and on quiet nights the walls of the world seem to lean closer.

slots.label: Ending: Hollow Victory
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Escape half-starved after a famine-ridden run.

What happens: You get out. Barely. Three skeletons wearing skin stumble into a sunrise that feels like an insult. The first meal on the surface is a stale roll, and it's the best thing you've ever eaten. Nobody mentions the … rotten meal…. Nobody mentions the days it was them or the rations.

slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:

What happens: You step into the sunlight, but the shadows stay long behind you. ${x.alive.length ?

slots.label: Ending: The Keeper
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Spend the Crown to call back the fallen, and stay below.

What happens: The Crown burns white in your hands. … … into the light of the surface, alive, confused, and furious with you before they even understand why. The seal closes behind them. You stay below, the new keeper of the Abyss. On certain nights the dungeon hums two voices, harmonizing, off-key.

slots.label: Ending: The Crowned Court
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Take the Crown with loyal companions at your side.

What happens: The monsters kneel. So do …, but only after you hold out your hand and they take it. The Abyss gets a court instead of a tyrant, and the surface world sleeps uneasy, never quite sure whether the Dark Lord's shadow is one shape or three.

slots.id: Cutscene: Ending: The Knife In The Dark
slots.label: Ending: The Knife In The Dark
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Take the Crown while a companion's trust has rotted away.

What happens: You wear the Crown for exactly one night. … comes into the throne room with a knife you once taught them to hold. "You were someone worth following, once." The Abyss gets a new master by morning. It isn't you.

slots.label: Ending: Crown Of One
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Take the Crown with no one left to stop you.

What happens: The Crown fits perfectly. There is no one left alive to tell you that it shouldn't. The monsters kneel, because they have never known anyone else. You rule the silence, and the silence rules you right back.

slots.label: Ending: The Hollow Crown
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Unlock the Final Gate with the Hollow Gate Key and put the Hollow King to rest, twice.

What happens: The portal closes behind you like a book. Above, the sky is exactly as large as you remembered. … The villages will tell it wrong: that something old was put to sleep, that a crown rolled and stopped. The truth is smaller. There was a king, and there was a hole in the world, and for once someone stood in front of it and did not look away. On the quietest nights you can still hear a choir finishing its last verse, and it sounds, at long last, like peace.

slots.label: Ending: Wren Comes Home
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Find Lyra’s sister at the last stair, free her from the song, and walk out with both sisters.

What happens: Two sisters come up the last stair holding hands, one of them still humming under her breath and unable to stop. Wren flinches at the sky for a whole day. Lyra doesn’t let go of her for longer than that. Bror stands behind them both like a wall, pretending he is not crying into his beard. Far below, without its singer, something turns over in its sleep, and finds the dark is quieter than it remembered. Somebody else will have to sing now. Not Wren. Never again Wren.

slots.label: Ending: The Forge Relit
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Relight the forge of Karak-Dun with Bror’s ember, and walk out with him.

What happens: Bror walks into the daylight carrying an empty tin. The ember is where it belongs: in the deep forge of Karak-Dun, burning for the first time in a century. When he climbs the mountain to tell his people, they don’t believe him, so he takes them down to see. With him, as he always said: Lyra and Bror. The singing in the deep falters every time the hammers ring. The dwarves ring them a lot.

slots.label: Ending: The Ledger Burns
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Defy the Gray Hand to their face, then smash the Crown.

What happens: You walk up to the Brass Gates with the shards of the Crown in a sack and drop it at Collector Harrow’s feet. “Your property,” you say. It is in pieces. It hums, very quietly, and then stops. That night the Gray Hand’s ledgers burn, and nobody can say who lit them. Nobody tries very hard. Lyra and Bror stand behind you through all of it.

slots.id: Cutscene: Ending: The Company Of The Deep
slots.label: Ending: The Company Of The Deep
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Walk out with Lyra, Bror and two or more delvers who trust you, without losing anyone.

What happens: Six, seven, eight of you come up out of the dark together, and the guards at the Brass Gates count you twice because nobody has ever come up in a crowd. Lyra, Bror, and the delvers who chose you: Lyra and Bror. You lost no one. The town will not believe it. You will tell it anyway, for years, at a long table, with everyone there to correct the details.

slots.id: Cutscene: Ending: Strangers At The Gate
slots.label: Ending: Strangers At The Gate
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Lose Lyra and Bror, but walk out with the delvers or Mira who stayed.

What happens: Lyra and Bror stayed in the dark: . The people who walk out with you are almost strangers: Lyra and Bror. You found them in the deep and they followed you up. At the gates nobody asks who they are to you. You would not know what to say. Family, maybe. The kind you make out of whoever is left.

slots.id: Cutscene: Ending: A Funeral In Daylight
slots.label: Ending: A Funeral In Daylight
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Lose three or more of your party along the way, and still lead someone out.

What happens: You hold the funeral in daylight, because they never got to see it. . A name for every stone. Lyra and Bror dig beside you, and nobody speaks until the last stone is set. Then someone tells a story about one of them, badly, and someone laughs, and it is the right way to end a funeral.

slots.id: Cutscene: Ending: The One They Feared
slots.label: Ending: The One They Feared
slots.note: Plays when you reach this ending
slots.info:
One of the 22 main endings.
How you get it: Leave with a fearsome reputation and a cruel name.

What happens: They open the Brass Gates for you without being asked. The guards look at the ground. The Gray Hand sends a man with a gift, and an apology for an old debt nobody can quite remember. Down in the deep, delvers tell your story to frighten each other. Up here, mothers do. Lyra and Bror walk behind you, a careful two steps back.

slots.label: Delver Brakka Ironvow
slots.info:
Brakka Ironvow. Shield of the Ironvow line. My father held a bridge for three days. I mean to hold something longer.
What they want: A bridge with my name on it. A real one, over a real river.
Their ending: Brakka holds the Brass Gates open with her shield for the last debtors coming up, and they name the bridge after her anyway.

slots.label: Delver Dolgrim Stonebeard
slots.info:
Dolgrim Stonebeard. I keep promises. That’s the whole introduction. It’s a long one if you’ve met me.
What they want: To keep the last promise I made before I came down: to come back.
Their ending: Dolgrim knocks on a door in Karak-Dun eleven years late. It opens.

slots.label: Delver Hilda Oreseeker
slots.info:
Hilda Oreseeker. I find silver. That’s not boasting, it’s a nose. I can smell it through granite.
What they want: Enough silver to never smell another vein as long as I live.
Their ending: Hilda finds the silver vein beneath Karak-Dun, and gives a share of it to every debtor’s family.

slots.label: Delver Torvek Deepdelver
slots.info:
Torvek Deepdelver. Rune-reader. I know which runes lie. People are harder.
What they want: A clean slate. People call me two-faced. I’d like to try having one.
Their ending: Torvek testifies against the Gray Hand on the surface, in his one honest face.

slots.label: Delver Nessa Anvilsong
slots.info:
Nessa Anvilsong. I sing to stone. It sings back, if you’re polite.
What they want: To sing in the open air, just once, and hear nothing answer.
Their ending: Nessa sings on a hilltop at dawn, and for once nothing answers. She cries, happily.

slots.label: Delver Aelindra Moonwhisper
slots.info:
Aelindra Moonwhisper. I was shooting before your grandmother was born. I’m not boasting, I’m explaining why I’m better than you.
What they want: To be remembered by someone who won’t die in fifty years.
Their ending: Aelindra carves the names of everyone in your party into an elven tree that will stand for a thousand years.

slots.label: Delver Thalion Verdanthil
slots.info:
Thalion Verdanthil. I don’t lie. It’s too much work remembering them.
What they want: To know what is under the last door. That’s all. Just to know.
Their ending: Thalion stands at the door of hands, and finally stops dreaming of it.

slots.label: Delver Sylvaris Dawnleaf
slots.info:
Sylvaris Dawnleaf. Even this was a forest once. I’m visiting an old friend.
What they want: To plant something down here that grows.
Their ending: A pale tree grows in the Stone Crypt from Sylvaris’s seed. Delvers sleep under it for years.

slots.label: Delver Erevan Starfall
slots.info:
Erevan Starfall. Knight, technically. Strategic retreat specialist, practically.
What they want: Just once, to not run.
Their ending: Erevan stands his ground once, at the very end, and lives to tell it badly.

slots.label: Delver Lirael Thornweave
slots.info:
Lirael Thornweave. I weave. Threads, spells, stories. Mostly the last one.
What they want: To choose which end of the thread I’m holding, for once.
Their ending: Lirael burns the Gray Hand’s copy of the Crown’s writ in the town square.

slots.label: Delver Vhaeryn Duskblade
slots.info:
Vhaeryn Duskblade. I’m loyal to whoever’s winning. Right now that’s you. Don’t lose.
What they want: To find someone worth losing for.
Their ending: Vhaeryn buys back his own name from the Gray Hand ledger with your share of the treasure, and never sells it again.

slots.label: Delver Zilvra Nightweave
slots.info:
Zilvra Nightweave. Gold is frozen starlight. I return it to the sky. Through my purse.
What they want: A sky full of starlight, and no one counting it.
Their ending: Zilvra robs the Gray Hand’s counting house, and the snow that winter is full of silver coins.

slots.label: Delver Drizzen Shadowmere
slots.info:
Drizzen Shadowmere. I never miss. I choose not to hit the people I like. For now.
What they want: To have more people I like than people I don’t.
Their ending: Drizzen spends his life guarding the people he once agreed to kill.

slots.label: Delver Malya Veilstep
slots.info:
Malya Veilstep. Yes, my people have a reputation. I’d like to spoil it.
What they want: To be trusted by someone who knows what I am.
Their ending: Malya is trusted by a whole town, and finds it exhausting and wonderful.

slots.label: Delver Ilnarith Voidcaller
slots.info:
Ilnarith Voidcaller. The dark and I are old acquaintances.
What they want: To find out whether the dark remembers me back.
Their ending: Ilnarith walks out into the sunlight and the dark finally lets go of his hand.

slots.label: Delver Garrick Holt
slots.info:
Garrick Holt. I took an oath once. I’ve been trying to keep it since.
What they want: To tell the man who gave me my oath that I kept it.
Their ending: Garrick tears up his oath on the Gray Hand’s steps and spends his life getting debtors out.

slots.label: Delver Marla Finch
slots.info:
Marla Finch. I patch people up and shoot what hurt them. Simple life.
What they want: A day when nobody needs patching.
Their ending: Marla opens a clinic by the Brass Gates for anyone who climbs out.

slots.label: Delver Edric Vane
slots.info:
Edric Vane. Knowledge is power, power is currency. I’m rich in theory.
What they want: To publish the first true map of the Abyss, and be paid enormously.
Their ending: Edric publishes his notes for free, and is furious about how famous it makes him.

slots.label: Delver Sera Blackwood
slots.info:
Sera Blackwood. My family name is on three monuments. I’d like a fourth.
What they want: A monument that names everyone who came down with me, not just me.
Their ending: Sera comes back, the first Blackwood who ever did, and refuses a statue.

slots.label: Delver Tobin Marsh
slots.info:
Tobin Marsh. Very brave. From a safe distance.
What they want: A safe distance from everything, forever.
Their ending: Tobin writes down everything he saw from the back, and it becomes the truest account of the Abyss.

slots.label: Delver Kharzul Emberscale
slots.info:
Kharzul Emberscale. My clan counts honour in scars. I’m nearly rich.
What they want: One scar for this place. A big one.
Their ending: Kharzul gets his scar at the last door and tells the true story of it to anyone who stands still.

slots.label: Delver Sorrek Ashmaw
slots.info:
Sorrek Ashmaw. The fire in me doesn’t lie. It can’t hold one.
What they want: To warm something that’s been cold for a long time.
Their ending: Sorrek lights the hearth of an abandoned house by the Brass Gates and keeps it burning for every debtor.

slots.label: Delver Vhorra Flamecrest
slots.info:
Vhorra Flamecrest. Watch the arrow. It burns on the way. Mine always do.
What they want: To shoot one arrow that matters more than the others.
Their ending: Vhorra’s burning arrow lights the dark at the last door, and everybody sees the way out.

slots.label: Delver Balasar Cindertail
slots.info:
Balasar Cindertail. Built like a wall. I decided to be a gentle one.
What they want: To carry someone out who couldn’t walk.
Their ending: Balasar carries the last injured debtor out of the Abyss on his back, and goes home gentle.

slots.label: Delver Rhogar Stormbreath
slots.info:
Rhogar Stormbreath. Dragons hoard. I hoard. It’s practically blood duty.
What they want: A hoard big enough to sleep on, like the old stories.
Their ending: Rhogar sleeps on a hoard of buttons, and one of them is yours.

slots.label: Delver Pip Underbough
slots.info:
Pip Underbough. Did you hear that? No? Good. I’ll listen for both of us.
What they want: A round door, a full pantry, and absolutely no adventures.
Their ending: Pip hears a terrible whistle in the deep halls, and follows it, and finds his cousin’s pack. He brings it home.

slots.label: Delver Rosie Thistledown
slots.info:
Rosie Thistledown. Bread, cheese, a kind word. That’s the whole of the great magic.
What they want: To feed everyone at a table that never runs out.
Their ending: Rosie opens an inn where every debtor eats free, forever.

slots.label: Delver Bramley Goodbarrel
slots.info:
Bramley Goodbarrel. A second breakfast is a right, and so is a second share.
What they want: Two breakfasts, every day, for the rest of my life.
Their ending: Bramley’s village pays his debt in loaves, and the Gray Hand has no choice but to accept.

slots.label: Delver Tansy Burrowby
slots.info:
Tansy Burrowby. I’d never steal from you. I’d only borrow without asking.
What they want: To give something back to everyone I borrowed from.
Their ending: Tansy spends her life returning things, and every return is a small celebration.

slots.label: Delver Fenwick Applewood
slots.info:
Fenwick Applewood. I keep a ledger of everything I owe. The page is long.
What they want: To close my ledger. Just once. To see the page empty.
Their ending: Fenwick burns his ledger in the sunlight, and laughs until he has to sit down.

slots.label: Mythic: Emberfang
slots.info:
A mythic item (weapon, greatsword).
A wyrm's tooth quenched in a forge that never went out.
Power: Cinder Cleave: The greatsword drags a line of fire across the foe.

slots.label: Mythic: Nightwhisper
slots.info:
A mythic item (weapon, dagger).
It is quiet in the way a held breath is quiet.
Power: Hush of Knives: A hundred small cuts, none of them seen.

slots.label: Mythic: Stormcaller
slots.info:
A mythic item (weapon, spear).
The haft hums before every storm.
Power: Thunderlance: The spear leaves your hand as thunder and returns as lightning.

slots.label: Mythic: Soulreaver
slots.info:
A mythic item (weapon, scythe).
Every name it has ever taken is still in the blade.
Power: Reap: The scythe takes what the foe has left and hands it to you.

slots.label: Mythic: Glacierbrand
slots.info:
A mythic item (weapon, sword).
Forged under a glacier that is still moving.
Power: Absolute Zero: The world holds still, and the foe holds still with it.

slots.label: Mythic: Bloodmoon Cleaver
slots.info:
A mythic item (weapon, axe).
It is warm. It is always warm.
Power: Crimson Feast: You drink the fight itself.

slots.label: Mythic: Judgement
slots.info:
A mythic item (weapon, hammer).
Law is only violence with a good memory.
Power: Verdict: The hammer falls once, and the sentence is carried out.

slots.label: Mythic: Echoing Gale
slots.info:
A mythic item (weapon, twin).
The second blade is only ever a half-second behind the first.
Power: Thousand Cuts: Five blows, one breath, and the wind still calling after.

slots.label: Mythic: Worldsplitter
slots.info:
A mythic item (weapon, axe).
It was made to cut mountains. Flesh is an afterthought.
Power: Quake: The ground opens under the blow.

slots.label: Mythic: Dawnbreaker
slots.info:
A mythic item (weapon, sword).
The first light the Deep ever saw was this edge.
Power: Sunburst: For one heartbeat the Deep is lit like noon.

slots.id: Mythic: Crown of the Drowned King
slots.label: Mythic: Crown of the Drowned King
slots.info:
A mythic item (helm, helm).
The water inside never drains.

slots.label: Mythic: Helm of Ashen Vigil
slots.info:
A mythic item (helm, helm).
Someone kept watch in it for four hundred years.

slots.label: Mythic: Visage of the Void
slots.info:
A mythic item (helm, mask).
It looks back, and it looks pleased.

slots.id: Mythic: Aegis of the Fallen Sun
slots.label: Mythic: Aegis of the Fallen Sun
slots.info:
A mythic item (armor, chest).
The sun fell, and this is what it left.

slots.label: Mythic: Wyrmscale Hauberk
slots.info:
A mythic item (armor, chest).
The wyrm that wore it first did not give it up.

slots.label: Mythic: Shroud of Midnight
slots.info:
A mythic item (armor, robe).
Light enters and does not come out.

slots.label: Mythic: Greaves of the Colossus
slots.info:
A mythic item (legs, legs).
You will stand wherever you are told to stand.

slots.label: Mythic: Trollking's Leggings
slots.info:
A mythic item (legs, legs).
They twitch when you are hurt, and then the hurt closes.

slots.label: Mythic: Windstrider Boots
slots.info:
A mythic item (boots, boots).
Your footprints arrive a moment after you do.

slots.id: Mythic: Sabatons of the Endless Road
slots.label: Mythic: Sabatons of the Endless Road
slots.info:
A mythic item (boots, boots).
The road has not ended, and neither will you.

slots.id: Mythic: Pendant of the Gilded Eye
slots.label: Mythic: Pendant of the Gilded Eye
slots.info:
A mythic item (neck, amulet).
It sees the price of everything.

slots.label: Mythic: Amulet of Second Dawn
slots.info:
A mythic item (neck, amulet).
Every morning is the second one.

slots.label: Mythic: Oracle's Tear
slots.info:
A mythic item (neck, drop).
It is not a tear. It is a window.

slots.label: Mythic: Wellspring Locket
slots.info:
A mythic item (neck, amulet).
Open it and something small is singing.

slots.label: Mythic: Deathward Talisman
slots.info:
A mythic item (neck, amulet).
Death has been asked to wait, and has agreed. For now.

slots.id: Mythic: Fang of the Berserker King
slots.label: Mythic: Fang of the Berserker King
slots.info:
A mythic item (neck, fang).
Wear it and remember how angry you used to be.

slots.id: Mythic: Clover of a Thousand Fortunes
slots.label: Mythic: Clover of a Thousand Fortunes
slots.info:
A mythic item (neck, clover).
There is one leaf too many. That is the lucky one.

slots.label: Mythic: Mindanchor Choker
slots.info:
A mythic item (neck, amulet).
The thoughts that go in circles go around it instead.

slots.label: Mythic: Heart of the Mountain
slots.info:
A mythic item (neck, drop).
It is very heavy and very slow, and nothing has ever moved it.

slots.label: Mythic: Eclipse Torc
slots.info:
A mythic item (neck, amulet).
A ring of gold around a hole where the sun should be.

slots.label: Mythic: Ring of Cinders
slots.info:
A mythic item (ring, ring).
Fire ring. Its stone is a live coal under glass.

slots.label: Mythic: Ring of the Tide
slots.info:
A mythic item (ring, ring).
Water ring. It rises and falls with your breathing.

slots.label: Mythic: Ring of Stone
slots.info:
A mythic item (ring, ring).
Earth ring. It does not care what happens to you.

slots.label: Mythic: Ring of Gales
slots.info:
A mythic item (ring, ring).
Air ring. Somewhere inside it, a wind is turning.

slots.label: Mythic: Ring of Thunder
slots.info:
A mythic item (ring, ring).
Storm ring. It is warm and smells of rain.

slots.label: Mythic: Ring of Frost
slots.info:
A mythic item (ring, ring).
Ice ring. Your breath fogs when you look at it.

slots.label: Mythic: Ring of Shadows
slots.info:
A mythic item (ring, ring).
Shadow ring. It casts a darker shadow than you do.

slots.label: Mythic: Ring of Radiance
slots.info:
A mythic item (ring, ring).
Light ring. It makes the room look kinder than it is.

slots.label: Mythic: Ring of the Void
slots.info:
A mythic item (ring, ring).
Void ring. There is nothing in the setting. That is the stone.

slots.label: Mythic: Ring of Verdant Growth
slots.info:
A mythic item (ring, ring).
Life ring. Moss has grown over the band and it is warm.

slots.label: Death Card: Death
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Black).
The Abyss keeps every name it takes. Someone down here has already written yours.

slots.label: Death Card: Danger
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Red).
Something is always watching from the dark. Trust the warning in your gut.

slots.label: Death Card: Loss
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Brown).
Not every friend walks out with you. Keep the ones who do close.

slots.label: Death Card: Guidance
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Yellow).
A light in the dark points the way. Follow it, even when it looks wrong.

slots.label: Death Card: Fortune
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (White).
Luck favours the bold. Sometimes gold simply finds its way to you.

slots.label: Death Card: Hunger
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Green).
Rations run thin, but the Abyss always has something to eat. So do you.

slots.label: Death Card: Final Toll
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Black).
A distant bell rings once for every soul the Abyss has swallowed. Listen closely. It is counting.

slots.label: Death Card: Ambush
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Red).
The quiet room is the loudest warning. Nothing waits this patiently without a reason.

slots.label: Death Card: Fallen Friend
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Brown).
A name scratched into the wall, a scrap of cloth, a boot. Someone came this far, and no further.

slots.label: Death Card: Lantern
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Yellow).
One small light, left burning by someone who wanted you to find the way. Carry it carefully.

slots.label: Death Card: Lucky Coin
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (White).
It lands on its edge, then falls your way. Do not ask why. Pocket it, and keep moving.

slots.label: Death Card: Gnawing Belly
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Green).
The ache is only a conversation. Feed it, or it will start making demands.

slots.label: Death Card: Silent Grave
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Black).
Not every grave is marked. Some rooms are simply quieter than the rest, and for good reason.

slots.label: Death Card: Tripwire
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Red).
A thread, thin as a hair, stretched across the dark. Someone wants you to step lightly. Or not at all.

slots.label: Death Card: Lost Road
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Brown).
The way you came is gone, and nobody can say when it went. Mark every turn you take.

slots.label: Death Card: Compass Rose
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Yellow).
The needle spins, settles, and points down. It is rarely wrong. It is rarely kind.

slots.label: Death Card: Open Door
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (White).
Every lock down here has a key. Sometimes the key is simply being the one who tried the handle.

slots.label: Death Card: Bitter Root
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Green).
It tastes of earth and regret, and it will keep you alive. Chew slowly. Swallow anyway.

slots.label: Death Card: Ashes
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Black).
Whatever burned here burned for a long time. Whatever is left no longer cares who you are.

slots.label: Death Card: Blood Moon
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Red).
There is no moon this deep, yet the walls glow red all the same. Something has noticed you.

slots.label: Death Card: Faded Memory
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Brown).
You almost remember a name, a face, a song. The dark keeps what you cannot hold.

slots.label: Death Card: Whispered Hint
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Yellow).
Someone, or something, murmurs the answer just before you need it. Do not turn to look.

slots.label: Death Card: Silver Lining
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (White).
The worst hour often hides a gift. Check your pockets, and your luck.

slots.label: Death Card: Famine
slots.info:
One of the 24 Death Cards (Green).
Nothing grows here, and nothing is spared. Count your rations twice, then count them again.
